sources.citation: Binam Bikoi, Charles (ed.). 2012. Atlas linguistique du Cameroun (ALCAM), vol. 1: Inventaire des langues. Yaoundé: CERDOTOLA (as summarised in Wikipedia 'Dii languages', which also cites Lars Lode 1997)
sources.note: Nothing on prosody. Dugun/Pa'no: c. 7,000 speakers (Lode 1997), southeast of Poli; Dugun in the plains, Saa in a massif; Lode estimated 95% lexical similarity between the two on a 100-word list; 'closely related to Dii, but distinct'. The tone marking described on that page (acute = high, grave = low, unmarked = mid) is the Dii orthography, not Dugun.
